mechanism.base: The hard overcomes the soft, the old texts say, and this is why metal overcomes wood. A blade is only a blade against something that resists it: timber gives the edge its reason, and the grain decides whether a stroke runs clean. Wood never fights the steel. It takes the shape the cut gives it and keeps growing around the wound, and that is how a forest turns a knife into a craft.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Wood, the blade has nothing to work on: all that edge and no timber. The force turns on whatever is nearest. Start one thing you can finish with your hands.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Wood, the blade goes blunt before the timber is through: every log begun, none of them split. Sleep before you start the next one.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Wood makes it grow, so what you build adds up. As a catalyst, the growth runs thin, and your hands have less to work on than they want. You build less than your strength could carry.
function.definition_friction: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Wood keeps it reaching, and building never feels done. As a friction, wanting outruns strength, and the work always asks for more than you have. You spend yourself faster than you refill.
function.definition_balanced: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Wood makes it grow, so what you build adds up. In balance, your hunger to build has strength under it. In a lean stretch, you slow down and still grow.
function.advise_catalyst: You get hardest on yourself when your strength has nothing to build. Give it something. Pick one venture this month and carry it to its first result. Plant one thing this week, a seed or a habit, and watch it grow.
function.advise_friction: Seek Metal, your own Body energy. Metal is your own core under the effort, what stays when the wanting stops. Let it trim what Wood spreads. You treat rest as time stolen from building. Drop one project you no longer believe in. Choose three things for this month and let the others wait.
function.advise_balanced: Your work keeps growing while each new start stays in step with your strength. Begin one new venture this month at a size you can tend. Plant one thing this week, a seed or a habit, and watch it grow.

candidates.cta_verdict: You want something to build more than something to be given, so you stay with what you made long after a gift would have bored you.

catalyst.clause: The blade has nothing to work on: all that edge and no timber.
catalyst.remedy: Start one thing you can finish with your hands.

friction.clause: The blade goes blunt before the timber is through: every log begun, none of them split.
friction.remedy: Sleep before you start the next one.

wide.clause: You have plenty of Wood, timber stacked as far as the blade reaches.
wide.remedy: Use it. Pick one log and split it today.

missing.clause: No timber for the blade at all: the edge stays clean and nothing gets made.
missing.remedy: Borrow timber: another person's project, one job you did not pick.

spared.clause: No timber pulling at a thin edge: nothing drains what the core needs to keep.
spared.remedy: Keep it that way. Rest the edge before you look for work.

thin.clause: A little Wood suits a thin blade: small jobs, each finished before the next.
thin.remedy: Keep the jobs small and sleep between them.

excess.clause: Wood this hard chips the blade: the more timber there is, the less edge survives the work.
excess.remedy: Eat, sleep, then one log at a time.

catalyst.clause: The point has nothing to work: skill idling without a piece worth it.

friction.clause: The cutting never stops: trays of half-set stones, a facet worn on material that never ends.
friction.remedy: Cut fewer stones, and finish them.

wide.clause: Wood is already here in plenty, the material the wheel is for.
wide.remedy: Cut what is already in front of you. Finish it.

mechanism_yin.base: The hard prevails over the soft, the classics say, and so metal governs wood. The engraver's point meets the grain, the fine saw meets the branch, and the wild green takes a shape it could not find alone. The cut is craft rather than ruin: rough stock becomes inlay, bramble becomes orchard, under a point that knows what to spare.
mechanism_yin.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the point has nothing to work: skill idling without a piece worth it. Your chart asks you to claim material. Pick one living ambition and start cutting.
mechanism_yin.friction_turn: Run heavy, the cutting never stops: trays of half-set pieces, a point worn on material that never ends. The fine tool dulls on quantity. Cut fewer pieces, and finish them.

__ore.retired_bonds_dip: Providing is your quiet love language: the pruned garden speaks for you.
__ore.retired_fn_body: The Drive is your action function: what you go get, build, and hold. With Wood running it, action in you wants living material: ventures that grow, skills that branch, assets with rings in them. You claim by shaping rather than seizing, and what you prune well becomes durable and yours. Aim the edge at growth worth decades, not stems worth days.
__ore.retired_base_personal: Your core is Metal, and Metal tames Wood: the knife prunes the branch. Wood is the living, growing material your edge exists to shape: projects, plans, property, ambitions with sap still in them. That is why Wood is your Action, the arena of what you build and claim. Every clean cut you make turns wild growth into something orchard-shaped and yours.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_catalyst:
Wood is your Action, and as a catalyst, it is where your discipline becomes results: projects, ventures, skills that grow with tending. You do best with one live build that rewards steady work, and worst with none.

Steady, productive, restless in idleness. Busy weeks calm you more than empty ones, a work in progress makes you feel most like yourself, and the moment nothing depends on you the steam goes out of everything else too.

Building is how you stay whole, so never be without a build. Keep one main project at all times and give it the first hour of the day, before anyone else gets you. Review it weekly. When it ends, start the next within a month.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_friction:
Wood is your Action, and as a friction, it is too many builds drawing on too little fuel: every open project takes a daily cut of attention whether you touch it or not. Progress spreads thin across all of them.

Ambitious, capable, scattered. The list of half-done things is long and each one carries a little guilt, and somehow starting a new project still feels easier than finishing an old one. Momentum keeps restarting from zero and calling it a fresh start.

Finishing is a deeper form of ambition than starting ever was. List everything open, close or complete the bottom half, and give one thing your best. One in, one out from now on. Count your weeks by completions.

backlog_dips_tg_pattern.order: What you grow becomes structure: the timber you raise ends up framing the rules you live in.
